heading: Words
body:
Each word below is explained where the guides first use it. This list keeps the short meanings in one place.

| Word | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Accessible name | The text that a screen reader says for a button, link or field: the text inside it, its `aria-label`, the element that `aria-labelledby` names, or its `<label>`. Without one, the build stops with `TY1336`. |
| API baseline | The API of the last release, saved by `ty api freeze` in `server/api-baseline.json`. A later build that breaks it without a new major version stops with `TY1338`. |
| Assertion | A check in a test case that fails the case when the result is wrong, such as `Assert.equals(1200, total)`, the Python `assert`, the Kotlin `check` or the Swift `precondition`. A test case without one proves nothing (`TY1339`). |
| Joint compilation | Compiling Groovy files and Java files in one step, so that each can use the classes of the other. Tachyon compiles a Groovy handler this way with its generated Java runtime. |
| Size budget | The most script and WebAssembly that one route may load, in kilobytes as sent (`tac.budgets.script`, `tac.budgets.webassembly`). Over it, a release build stops with `TY1337`. |
| Field case | The way a language writes the name of a variable or a field: lowerCamel case (`cartStore`) in JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Groovy, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, Go and PHP, snake_case (`cart_store`) in Python, Ruby and Rust, and `_cartStore` for a private C# field. A field that holds an injected class uses it, or the build stops with `TY1332`. |
| `ty` | The one program that creates, previews, builds, tests and serves a Tachyon app. |
| Access rule | The annotation that says who may call a route: `@Public`, `@SignedIn` or `@Allow(Role)`. A route without one stops the build with `TY1322`. |
| Annotation | A marker on a class, a field or a method, such as `@Service`. It tells Tachyon what to do. |
| Binaryen | A set of WebAssembly tools. Its `wasm-opt` program makes a finished WebAssembly module smaller. A release build runs it on Rust, Go, Swift, Kotlin and Java modules when it is installed (see WebAssembly compilers per language). |
| Browser API | A feature of the browser, such as the clock or random numbers. Tachyon gives every Tac service a small set of them, such as `Clock`, `Connectivity` and `Geolocation`, through `@Needs`. |
| Browser API grant | A name in `tac.browserApis` in `client/manifest.json`, such as `clipboard`. `Clipboard`, `Share`, `Notifications` and `Geolocation` work only when the project grants them. |
| Browser interop | Code in another language than JavaScript or TypeScript that calls the browser directly, such as Go's `syscall/js`. Tachyon refuses it in Tac code (`TY1317`). |
| BrowserFakes | In a Go, Ruby, Lua or Swift test unit, the answers that Tachyon's browser APIs give, because a test unit has no page. `BrowserFakes{}.Answer("clock", "now", 1000)` makes `Clock` answer 1000. |
| Compressed copy | A `.br` (Brotli) or `.gz` (gzip) file that a release build writes next to a script, style, page, data or WebAssembly file. `ty start` sends it to a browser that accepts it, and the browser unpacks it to the same bytes. |
| Built-in event model | An event model that Tachyon declares for you, such as `ConnectivityChanged` or `PositionFound`. The page publishes it; a listener uses it like any model, without a file in `client/models/`. |
| Bundle | The built files of your app that you publish. `ty bundle` makes them. |
| Cohesion | How closely the code of one method belongs together. In a cohesive service, a public method only coordinates, and each private method does one small job. |
| Component | In a template, a part of a page that you can use again: a folder in `client/components` with a `tac.html` file. As an annotation, `Component` marks a helper class. |
| Controller | A class in `server/controllers` that answers HTTP requests. |
| Coverage | The public methods of annotated classes that a test case really called while `ty test` ran. A call on a Fake does not count. `ty preview` lists a method that was not called in its error box (`TY2023`), and `ty test --coverage` fails on it. |
| Decision | A place where code chooses a path: `if`, `switch`, a ternary, `&&`, `||`, `??`, `catch`, or a loop. |
| Dependency | A class that another class needs, because it names it in a field, a `Needs` list or its code. Dependencies point down, and no chain of them may loop back (`TY1327`). |
| Duplicated code | A block of code that appears twice or more, even with other names or values. Tachyon refuses it with `TY1315`. |
| Error box | The box that `ty preview` shows on top of open pages when a build fails: each problem with its code, message, file and line, and help. It has a Dismiss button, and it goes away after the next good build. |
| Error page | The page that `ty preview` serves when the project has a problem at start. It lists the problems and opens the site as soon as the project builds. |
| Event | A message that one service publishes and other services receive. |
| Field | A value that belongs to an object, such as `count` in a service. |
| Generated folder | `.tachyon` in the project and `dist/.tachyon` in the build. Tachyon writes them again when it needs them, so you can delete them at any time. They hold no saved data. |
| Helper | A class in `client/helpers` or `server/helpers` marked `@Helper`. Services use it for part of their work. Tachyon creates it and gives it to them through `Needs`. See Helpers, utilities and private methods. |
| Identity provider | The one class marked `@IdentityProvider`. Its method `identify` reads the request and says who is signed in and which roles they have. |
| Last good build | The newest build that succeeded. When a save breaks the build, `ty preview` keeps serving it and shows the error box. |
| Layer | A level of the app: entry points (controllers and views), services, helpers, and data access (stores, repositories and clients). A class needs only classes of its own layer or a lower one. |
| Lifecycle hook | A method that runs when an object starts (`OnStart`) or stops (`OnStop`). |
| Magic value | A text or number written in the code without a name, used twice, or a number in a condition. Tachyon asks for a class constant instead (`TY1330`). |
| Middleware | Code that runs before every request and after every response. |
| Model | A data type that describes the shape of a value, such as a product. It lives in `client/models` or `server/models`, one model in each file, and the file is named after it. In every Tac language, a service field, a list field and a method argument can hold a model, and a model can hold other models. |
| Native host | The desktop or mobile app that Tachyon builds for a target. |
| Page | A `tac.html` file under `client/pages`. Its folder decides its URL. |
| Plain state | A field with a starting value, such as `count = 0`. Tachyon never fills it, and it may stay empty. |
| Private member | A method or field that only its own class uses. Each language has its own private form, such as `private` or a name that starts with `_`. A member stays public only when a view, another class or Tachyon uses it (`TY1333`). |
| Realm | One side of the app. Tac is the frontend realm, and Yon is the backend realm. |
| Required field | A field that Tachyon fills before any method runs: a `Needs` field, or a `NeedsAll` field without a starting value. It is never null, so it uses the language's non-null form, such as `name!: string` or `late final String name;`. A nullable one stops the build with `TY1331`. |
| Role | The job of a class, such as service, controller or store. The role decides the folder of the file. |
| Route | A path and an HTTP verb that a controller method answers, such as GET /products. |
| Secret | A value that gives access, such as a password, a token or a key. It lives in `.env`, never in the code (`TY1324`). |
| Service | In Tac, a class in `client/services` that holds the data and the actions of a view. In Yon, a class in `server/services` that controllers use. |
| Setup | The class that gives named adapters (caches, HTTP, entities and the authorization hooks) from its `configure` method, like a Spring `@Configuration`. Tachyon configures it once per page in Tac and once per server process in Yon, so every behavior context built from it shares the same adapters. |
| Signature | The name of a method and its parameters. A method takes at most 4 parameters (`TY1329`). |
| Simpler form | A way to write the same code that reads more plainly, such as `items.some(isReady)` instead of `items.filter(isReady).length > 0`. `ty build`, `ty preview` and `ty test` show it as a suggestion (`TY1340` to `TY1355`), which never stops the build. |
| Socket | A WebSocket: a connection that stays open, so both sides can send messages at any time. |
| SSRF | Server-side request forgery: a caller makes your server send a request to an address that they choose. Tachyon allows only the hosts that you list (`TY1326`). |
| Store | A contract that names an Entity and declares its queries, like a Spring Data repository interface. Tachyon writes each query, and a service asks for the store with Needs in Yon and in Tac. |
| Stream | One HTTP answer that stays open and sends many messages (server-sent events). |
| Tac | The frontend part of Tachyon: pages, components and services. |
| Target | The kind of app that you build: web, macos, windows, linux, ios or android. |
| Test case | A method of a test unit whose name begins with `test`. It prepares values, calls the code and checks the result with `Assert` or the assert of its language, with no branch or loop (`TY1339`). With `ValueSource`, Tachyon runs it once for each input. |
| Test unit | A class whose name ends with `Test`. `ty test` runs it. |
| Topic | A model marked `@Topic`. Tachyon saves each published value in the topic log and sends it to the listeners in every Yon language and in open pages. |
| Topic log | The file that keeps the values of one topic, one JSON line each: `data/topics/<name>.jsonl`, or the folder that `topics.directory` in `server/application.json` names. It is saved data, so back it up. |
| Type comment | A comment that a tool reads for the type of a field, parameter or return value, in a language whose syntax has no types: JSDoc `@param {number} amount` in JavaScript, YARD `# @param amount [Integer]` in Ruby and LuaCATS `---@param amount integer` in Lua. It holds a type, never an explanation. Every member of a class has a type (`TY1356`). |
| Utility class | A class in `client/utils` or `server/utils` with only static methods and no state. Code that would repeat lives there, and every class of the realm can call it. |
| View | The `tac.html` file of a page or a component. |
| WebAssembly | A compiled format that browsers run. Rust, Go, C#, F#, Swift, Kotlin, Java and Dart services use it in the browser, and Ruby and Lua services run on an interpreter compiled to it. Dart, Kotlin and Java need WasmGC, WebAssembly with garbage collection (Chrome or Edge 119, Firefox 120, Safari 18.2 and newer). |
| Primary constructor | In F#, the parameter list written right after the type name, as in `type OrderService(orderStore: OrderStore) =`. Tachyon fills these parameters with the roles they name, so an F# type takes its dependencies, its `DataSource` and its `ApplicationEventPublisher` there. It is the recommended form; a Needs property is the other one. `[<NeedsAll>]` on the type states this; in a Tac service it also makes the parameters take the component's properties, as in `type SnippetService(files: string list) =` (ADR 0073). |
| WebView | The browser view that is built into the operating system. A native host shows your pages in it. |
| Yon | The backend part of Tachyon: controllers, services and stores on the server. |
| TinyGo | A Go compiler for small devices and WebAssembly. It leaves out most of the Go runtime, so a Go service module is many times smaller. A release build uses it first for Go web services (`tac.go.compiler`). |
| TeaVM | A compiler from Java bytecode to JavaScript and WebAssembly. Tachyon compiles Java web services with its WebAssembly garbage collection (WasmGC) backend; `ty doctor --install` downloads its jars into the Tachyon cache, or `TAC_TEAVM_HOME` names a folder of your own. |
| Abstract member | In F#, a member written with `abstract` and no body, as in `abstract findByStatus: status: BehaviorJSON -> Task<BehaviorJSON>`. When it holds Query, Convert, Gateway or a request annotation, Tachyon writes its body during the build. |
| Contract | A declaration with no implementation, such as a Java `interface`, a Rust `trait`, a Swift `protocol` or a Python `Protocol` class. An `HTTPClient` and a `Store` are contracts: Tachyon generates each request and each query, and a body in them stops the build with `TY1308`. JavaScript, TypeScript and Ruby write a class whose methods have empty bodies instead. |
| Embedded Swift | A small form of Swift for tiny devices, without `Codable`, `Any` values and `as?` casts. Tachyon does not use it for Swift services on the web, because services need those parts. |
| Transaction | A group of changes that all happen or all do not happen. AllOrNothing opens one on a service method, and a store that the method calls joins it. |
| Custom element | A tag that JavaScript defines with `customElements.define`, such as `<shop-counter>`. Its name must contain a hyphen. A component listed in `tac.elements` becomes one, so other apps can use it (`TY1358`). |
| Shadow DOM | A separate tree of elements inside an element. The styles of the page do not reach inside it, except inherited values and CSS custom properties. An exported component draws its view there. |
| LuaCATS | The type comments that the Lua language server reads, such as `---@param id integer`, `---@return Order[]` and `---@class Order` with `---@field name string`. Lua writes every type of a class this way (`TY1356`). |
| Class table | In Lua, the one global table of a class file, such as `OrderService = {}`. Its methods are `function OrderService:list()`, and Tachyon makes each object with the table as its metatable (ADR 0085). In a Tac service, each object also starts with its own copy of the table's fields. |
| Repository | The base that a Store can extend, like Spring Data's `CrudRepository`: `Repository<Entity, Id>` gives the store `findById`, `findAll`, `save` and `deleteById` without declaring them. |
| Derived delete | A Store method whose name starts with `deleteBy` (or `delete_by_`). It removes every record that its predicates match and answers how many it removed. |
| Declaration file | A TypeScript file that ends in `.d.ts` and describes types without any code. The build writes one beside each exported element, so a TypeScript page knows its tag, props and events. |
| Slot | A place in a component template where the children of the component show. `<slot>` takes the children without a `slot` attribute; a named slot, such as `<slot name="title">`, takes the children with `slot="title"` (`TY1404`). |
| Content Security Policy | A response header that lists what a page may load and run, such as scripts from other sites or WebAssembly. |
| Needs property | In F#, a settable property marked `[<Needs>]`, as in `[<Needs>] member val OrderStore : OrderStore = Unchecked.defaultof<OrderStore> with get, set`. Tachyon sets it right after the primary constructor runs, like a Spring field, and `[<Named("...")>]` chooses another provider. A type may not take one role both as a constructor parameter and as a Needs property (`TY2015`). |
| Converter | A contract whose Convert methods copy fields from one JSON value into a new one by a literal field plan, like a MapStruct mapper interface. It needs no behavior context, so Tachyon builds it with no constructor argument, and a service or controller asks for it with Needs in Yon and in Tac. |
| Public read | A `Cached` GET that a JavaScript or TypeScript `HTTPClient` sends without credentials and without `no-store`, so the service worker may answer it by the `tac.cache` rules of its path (ADR 0087). |
| WindowControls | The browser API for the native app window: `granted`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `fullscreen`, `close`, `resize` and `setTitle`. A service injects it, and `tac.application.window.controls` grants each control (ADR 0087). |
| Lua web runtime | Tachyon's Lua 5.4 interpreter, compiled to WebAssembly. Your machine builds it once from the pinned lua.org source with Emscripten, into the Tachyon cache, and every Tac Lua service of a page runs on it (ADR 0085). |
